translation.text: Blessed are you, O Lord, great King and mighty in your greatness, Lord of all heavenly creation[a], King of kings and God of all the world. Your sovereign power[b], your kingdom, and your greatness endure forever and ever, and your authority endures through every generation. All the heavens are your throne forever, and the whole earth is the footstool of your feet forever and ever.[c]

footnotes.text: Literally all the creation of heaven; heavenly creation is a compact rendering of the selected wording.

Sovereign power renders the selected printed መለኮትከ. Dillmann’s1865 lexicon,column152, gives divine dominion/power and directly cites84:2; it also lists divinity/deity as another sense. The present LOW-confidence reading of Charles’s edited print follows direct letter-form comparison, not replacement of unclear letters by the dictionary head. It does not certify an ancient manuscript spelling. The authority clause has no second written verb; English carries endures over from the preceding clause.

The source preserves the photographed throne form ምንበርከ, beginning with ም rather than normalized initial መ; Charles’s printed161note37 records alternative forms. Throne follows the seat/place noun family in Dillmann,columns654-655. Footstool follows the actual lexical entry in column873, which directly cites84:2; the wording of another biblical passage has not been used to fill this text. The forever-and-ever formulas are retained from both printed pages. These are bounded interpretations of the selected edited print, not claims of independent manuscript certainty.
